summary: Follow-up of the accepted parent plan for GC.3 (symmetric local systems on root symmetric powers, after Yun–Zhang Appendix A.2.1). It discharges the parent gap EXTERIOR-COMP with the Koszul-signed permutation action on Tau Ceti's reindexRepresentation, compatibility of the existing antisymmetrization with that action and the comparison of Koszul-signed invariants with the exterior power, all stated in Lean at the pins, together with rational averaging, finite-group acyclicity and the tensor-character lemma. It replaces the parent's stack sheaf operations by two routes: the symmetric local system is built from its monodromy on the distinct-point locus and extended by purity, and its cohomology is computed on the coarse symmetric power, where Künneth, duality and curve bounds are scheme statements with accepted suppliers. The stack inputs that remain are narrowed to three precise gaps for the proposed stacks Part II of EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves. The twelve parent GC.3 nodes are imported unchanged by id. This is a complete planning pass; GC.3 is planned, not closed. Current-library imports are recorded separately from the older pinned baseline: the exterior projection, factorial identities and naturality are already implemented and are not new construction targets.

nodes.title: Koszul-signed permutation action on tensor powers
nodes.statement: Let K be a commutative ring, V a K-module and d≥0. The Koszul-signed action of S_d=Perm({1,…,d}) on the tensor power V^{⊗d} sends σ to sgn(σ)·P_σ, where P_σ(v_1⊗⋯⊗v_d)=v_{σ⁻¹(1)}⊗⋯⊗v_{σ⁻¹(d)} is Tau Ceti's permutation representation PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation. It is a representation of S_d by K-linear maps, natural in V. It is the S_d-action on the degree-d summand of the graded tensor power of a graded module concentrated in cohomological degree one: exchanging two factors of odd degree contributes −1. On a tensor power of degree-zero factors the same permutation acts by P_σ, without sign.
hypotheses: K is a commutative ring, V any K-module and d a natural number.
In GC.3 the case used is K=Q̄ℓ and V=H¹(X⊗k̄,j_*L)≅H¹(X_1^√R⊗k̄,L), on which geometric Frobenius acts K-linearly.
proofSteps: P_σ is the reindexing of the tensor factors along σ, and σ↦P_σ is already a representation (tauceti:PiTensorProduct.reindexRepresentation).
sgn:S_d→{±1} is a homomorphism with values in the centre of End_K(V^{⊗d}), so σ↦sgn(σ)P_σ is again a representation.

For a K-linear f:V→W, use mathlib:PiTensorProduct.map_reindex to commute f^{⊗d} with P_σ, then with its sign twist. The Tau Ceti commute_reindexRepresentation_map citation covers the endomorphism case only.
acceptance: For d=2 and V=K the transposition acts on K⊗K≅K by −1, while P_σ alone acts by +1.
For d≤1 the group S_d is trivial and the action is the identity.

nodes.title: Koszul-signed invariants are the exterior power
nodes.statement: Let K be a commutative ring in which d! is invertible and V a K-module. The antisymmetrization α_d is an isomorphism from ∧^dV onto the invariants (V^{⊗d})^{S_d} of the Koszul-signed action, with inverse (d!)⁻¹·π_d restricted to the invariants. The isomorphism is natural in V, hence commutes with any K-linear Frobenius. Consequences: for d=0 both sides are K; for d=1 both are V; if V is free of rank n the invariants are free of rank C(n,d), in particular zero for d>n. Over K=Q̄ℓ, a field of characteristic zero, d! is invertible for every d, including when the prime ℓ divides d!.
hypotheses: K commutative ring with d! a unit; V any K-module (no finiteness needed for the isomorphism).
The rank statement assumes V free of finite rank n and K nontrivial.
proofSteps: α_d lands in the invariants and π_d∘α_d=d!·id (GC.3/antisymmetrization), so α_d is injective when d! is a unit.

Reuse the current-library identity α_d∘π_d=Σ_σ sgn(σ)P_σ (currentLibraryImports). For an invariant tensor t this is Σ_σ σ_Koszul(t)=d!·t, giving the inverse (d!)⁻¹π_d. The companion identity π_d∘α_d=d!·id proves injectivity.
Naturality is that of α_d and π_d; the rank follows from mathlib:exteriorPower.finrank_eq, C(n,d)=0 for d>n.
acceptance: d=2, V of rank 2: the invariants are spanned by e_1⊗e_2−e_2⊗e_1, of rank 1=C(2,2).
dim V=1, d=2: the invariants are zero, while the unsigned (symmetric) invariants would be the whole line.
Over Z/2, d=2, V=Z/2: the statement fails (invariants the whole line, ∧²=0), so the hypothesis on d! cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: Rational averaging: invariants are exact and commute with linear functors
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite group and K a commutative ring in which |G| is invertible. (i) For a K-linear representation V, e_V=|G|⁻¹Σ_{g∈G}g is an idempotent with image V^G, and V↦V^G is exact: an equivariant surjection is surjective on invariants. (ii) In a K-linear additive category in which idempotents split (for example any abelian category, such as constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaves on a scheme), the invariants A^G of an object with a G-action are the image of e_A, and every K-linear additive functor F satisfies F(A^G)≅F(A)^G naturally, because F(e_A)=e_{F(A)}. In particular H^i(Y,A^G)≅H^i(Y,A)^G for a sheaf A with a G-action on a scheme Y, and q_* of invariants is the invariants of q_*.
hypotheses: G finite; |G| a unit in K. Over Q̄ℓ this holds for every finite G, including groups of order divisible by ℓ.
proofSteps: e is fixed by left and right multiplication by G and e²=e (mathlib:GroupAlgebra.average); its image is V^G (mathlib:Representation.isProj_averageMap; tauceti:Representation.range_norm_eq_invariants).
Exactness: if f:V→W is equivariant and onto and w∈W^G, choose v with f(v)=w; then e_V(v) is invariant and f(e_V v)=e_W(w)=w.

A preadditive category in which idempotents have kernels, for example an abelian category, is idempotent complete (mathlib:CategoryTheory.Idempotents.isIdempotentComplete_iff_idempotents_have_kernels); any additive functor preserves split idempotents and their images (Stacks §12.4), and K-linearity gives F(e_A)=e_{F(A)}.
acceptance: G=S_2 swapping the coordinates of K² with 2 invertible: the invariants are the diagonal and e(x,y)=((x+y)/2,(x+y)/2).
Without invertibility exactness fails: for G=Z/2 over Z/2, the augmentation (Z/2)[G]→Z/2 is onto but sends the invariant 1+g to 0, so the trivial invariant 1 is not hit.

sources.match: In the complex-representation setting, the proof identifies the group average as the projector onto invariants. The general ring case here follows from the same finite-sum calculation with |G| invertible, using the pinned averaging API.
For a finite group of order prime to the residue characteristics the averaging operator is a projector exhibiting the invariants as a direct summand, which gives base change of invariants.

nodes.title: Rational acyclicity of finite groups
nodes.statement: Let G be a finite group and M a G-module on which multiplication by |G| is bijective, for example a Q̄ℓ-vector space with a linear G-action. Then H^r(G,M)=0 for every r>0, and H^0(G,M)=M^G is the image of the averaging idempotent. Applied to the finite stabilizers of a tame Deligne–Mumford stack and to the kernel of μ₂^m→μ₂, this is the rational finite-groupoid cohomology vanishing used for collision fibres and for the coarse pushforward.
hypotheses: G finite; |G| acts bijectively on M. No condition relating |G| to ℓ is needed for Q̄ℓ-vector spaces.
proofSteps: Reuse the ordinary all-degree annihilation theorem groupCohomology.natCard_nsmul_eq_zero from current Tau Ceti (currentLibraryImports). Its transfer input is TauCeti.groupCohomology.map_subtype_id_comp_corestriction: Cor∘Res through the trivial subgroup is multiplication by |G| (Milne, CFT II.1.30–1.31). ProfiniteCohomology Layer 10 is the existing owner of transfer; the proof here uses the implemented ordinary theorem directly. Layer 3 only compares degrees 0–2, so it is not an all-degree comparison input.
H^r(1,M)=0 for r>0, so |G| kills H^r(G,M) (Milne, CFT II.1.31); |G| also acts bijectively on H^r(G,M) because it does on M, so H^r(G,M)=0.
Degree zero is GC.3/averaging-exactness.
acceptance: G=μ₂ acting on Q̄ℓ by the sign: H^r=0 for all r≥0, including H^0.
G=Z/2 acting trivially on F_2: H^r(G,F_2)=F_2 for every r, so the hypothesis cannot be dropped.

nodes.title: The tensor character factors through multiplication
nodes.statement: Let A be a commutative group, χ:A→Q̄ℓ^× a character and m≥1. The character (a_i)↦∏χ(a_i) of A^m is χ∘μ_m, where μ_m is multiplication, so it is trivial on N_m=ker μ_m and invariant under permutations. This algebraic assertion needs no finiteness. If A is finite, the derived N_m-invariants of this line are concentrated in degree zero and the quotient A^m/N_m≅A acts by χ. In GC.3 use A=μ₂(k̄). The translation into pushforward along B(A^m)→B(A), and the geometric stalk at n·x, is made only in GC.3/pushforward-description-comparison, using GC3-STACK-PUSHFORWARD; it is not a consequence of character algebra alone.
hypotheses: A is a commutative group and χ a homomorphism; m≥1.
The cohomological corollary assumes A finite and Q̄ℓ coefficients. Without finiteness, rational higher group cohomology need not vanish.
proofSteps: Because χ is a homomorphism and A is commutative, ∏χ(a_i)=χ(∏a_i) (mathlib:map_prod).

For finite A, N_m is finite and acts trivially on the line. Its invariants are that line and its higher rational cohomology vanishes by GC.3/finite-group-rational-acyclicity; the surjection μ_m (m≥1) identifies the quotient action with χ.
A permutation of the factors fixes ∏χ(a_i), and on L_x^{⊗n} it acts by the identity because the line is in degree zero.

nodes.title: Local systems on the root curve and inertia of order two
nodes.statement: Let 𝒳=X_1^√R and let ū be a geometric point of U⊂𝒳. Restriction to U is fully faithful from Q̄ℓ-local systems on 𝒳 to Q̄ℓ-local systems on U. Its essential image consists of the local systems whose monodromy, restricted to the inertia subgroup I_x̄⊂π1(U,ū) of every geometric point x̄ of X above R (for one, equivalently every, path), has order dividing two. In rank one: rank-one local systems on 𝒳 correspond to continuous characters χ:π1(U,ū)→Q̄ℓ^× of the arithmetic fundamental group over k with χ(τ)²=1 for all τ in every I_x̄. Such χ is tamely ramified at R, since the wild inertia is pro-p with p odd. The global monodromy is unrestricted: an unramified χ of order three, or of infinite order, is allowed. At a geometric point of 𝒳 over x∈R the stabilizer μ₂ acts on the stalk through χ|I_x̄, which is trivial or the character of order two; χ|I_x̄ is trivial for every x exactly when the local system descends to X.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

Local systems are lisse Q̄ℓ-sheaves of finite rank. π1(𝒳) is the fundamental group of the Galois category of representable finite étale covers of the Deligne–Mumford curve 𝒳 (Noohi §4), and local systems on 𝒳 are continuous representations of it (gap GC3-STACK-PI1). The stacks and atlas charts used here are normal. Coefficient objects are defined over a finite extension E/Qℓ before scalar extension to Q̄ℓ; no representation dictionary is asserted for arbitrary nonnormal stacks.
proofSteps: U is a dense open substack of the connected normal Deligne–Mumford curve 𝒳 (RS.1/regular-dm), so π1(U,ū)→π1(𝒳,ū) is surjective (IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas); restriction of continuous representations along a surjection is fully faithful.

Étale-locally at x∈R with local equation s, 𝒳 is [Spec A[t]/(t²−s)/μ₂] (RS.1/affine-chart, SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.1/root-stack). A local system on U extends over this chart exactly when its pullback to the double cover t²=s extends; the tame inertia of the double cover at t=0 is the subgroup of squares of the tame inertia at x (IG.1/tame-and-prime-to-p, IG.1/decomposition-inertia), so the pullback is unramified in codimension one exactly when the inertia image has order dividing two (Abhyankar's lemma, Stacks 0EYG).

A finite étale cover of the punctured regular chart that is unramified in codimension one extends uniquely to a finite étale cover of the chart (Stacks 0H2W); the extension is μ₂-equivariant by uniqueness and descends along the atlas (gap GC3-STACK-PI1).

The stabilizer μ₂ at x is the image of the local inertia, so it acts on the stalk by χ|I_x̄. By Noohi Theorem 7.11 the quotient of π1(𝒳) by the closed normal subgroup generated by the stabilizers is π1(X), which gives the descent criterion.
acceptance: R=∅: 𝒳=X and the statement is the ordinary dictionary between local systems on X and representations of π1(X).
X=P¹, R={0,∞}: over k̄, 𝒳≅[P¹/μ₂] for the squaring map, and the admissible geometric characters are the trivial one and the quadratic Kummer character of t ramified at 0 and ∞.
A character whose inertia at some x∈R has order four is excluded; one with χ(Frob)=ζ₃ and trivial geometric monodromy is admitted.

nodes.title: Symmetric local systems by descent and lisse extension
nodes.statement: Let L be a rank-one Q̄ℓ-local system on X_1^√R with character χ (GC.3/root-curve-character-dictionary) and d≥0. (i) The external product L^{⊠d}=pr_1^*L⊗⋯⊗pr_d^*L on (U^d)°, with the S_d-linearization that permutes tensor factors without sign, descends along the finite étale Galois S_d-cover (U^d)°→U_d° to a rank-one local system L_d° on U_d°. Over k̄ its monodromy is YZ19 (A.6): π1((U_d°)_k̄)→π1(U_k̄)^d⋊S_d→Q̄ℓ^×, (g_1,…,g_d;σ)↦∏χ(g_i), with χ valued in Q̄ℓ^× (EGC3-4). (ii) L_d° extends to a rank-one local system 𝕃_d on the smooth connected Deligne–Mumford stack X_d^√R, and the extension with its identification on U_d° is unique up to unique isomorphism. 𝕃_0 is the constant line on Spec k, 𝕃_1=L, and 𝕃_d carries the Frobenius descent datum of the construction over k. At a geometric point D=Σn_x x the stalk is one-dimensional and the stabilizer factor μ₂ at x∈R∩supp D acts through the inertia character of L at x. Notation: U=X−R with j:U→X; X_d=Sym^dX with the finite quotient map q_d:X^d→X_d; U_d°⊂X_d is the open of multiplicity-free divisors supported in U and (U^d)°=q_d⁻¹(U_d°) the ordered distinct points of U; ω_d:X_d^√R→X_d is the coarse map (GC.1/root-symmetric-coarse), an isomorphism over Sym^dU, so U_d° is open in X_d^√R.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
No pushforward along the nonrepresentable ordered map p_d is used; the comparison with the definition (p_{d,!}L^{⊠d})^{S_d} is GC.3/pushforward-description-comparison.
proofSteps: (U^d)°→U_d° is finite étale and Galois with group S_d, and Q̄ℓ-local systems form an étale stack (IG.0/adic-local-systems), so S_d-equivariant local systems descend (IG.0/etale-fundamental-group).

The complement of U_d° in X_d^√R is the union of the collision divisor Δ (two points of U meet) and the divisors D_x, x∈R, of root divisors containing x, plus a closed subset of codimension at least two.

Along Δ: near a generic point the S_d-cover is the quotient by one transposition of a smooth neighbourhood of the diagonal, and the transposition exchanges two equal lines L_y⊗L_y without sign, hence acts trivially; L_d° is unramified along Δ.
Along D_x: near a generic point, X_d^√R is étale-locally X_1^√R near x times U_{d−1}°, and L_d° is L⊠L_{d−1}°; L is a local system on X_1^√R, so L_d° extends over the generic point of D_x.

On an étale atlas of X_d^√R by a smooth scheme (GC.1/root-symmetric-smooth), the finite étale covers trivializing the finite-level reductions of L_d° are unramified in codimension one, so they extend (Stacks 0H2W, purity 0BMB); uniqueness of such extensions gives descent data on the atlas (gap GC3-STACK-PI1).

Uniqueness follows from full faithfulness on the dense open of the connected normal stack (IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas). For the stabilizer character, the boundary divisor of divisors containing a fixed geometric x is smooth and connected (GC.1/root-symmetric-smooth, YZ19 Lemma A.4, pp. 516–517). Its μ₂-action on a lisse line is locally constant, so is determined at the generic boundary point, where the product chart L⊠L_{d−1}° gives exactly χ|I_x. This remains true at n·x and at intersections of boundary divisors. This argument uses no pushforward comparison.

For f:L→L′, descend f^{⊠d} on the distinct-point locus and extend the map by full faithfulness. This gives map, identity and composition, with scalar a acting by a^d. The empty tensor power gives the identity when d=0, even for f=0.
acceptance: 𝕃_0=Q̄ℓ on X_0^√R=Spec k and 𝕃_1=L.
R=∅ and L constant give 𝕃_d constant on X_d.
With the Koszul-signed linearization the descended system has monodromy −1 around Δ and does not extend: the unsigned linearization is forced.

nodes.title: The coarse symmetric-power sheaf
nodes.statement: For L with character χ as above, let F=j_*(L|U), a constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaf on X with stalk F_x=L_x̄ at x∈U, F_x=L_x̄ at x∈R where the inertia character is trivial, and F_x=0 at x∈R where it is the sign. Define 𝓜_d=(q_{d*}F^{⊠d})^{S_d} on X_d=Sym^dX: the S_d-invariants, for the unsigned permutation of the tensor factors and of the coordinates of X^d, of the pushforward along the finite map q_d of F^{⊠d}=pr_1^*F⊗⋯⊗pr_d^*F. It is a constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaf with Frobenius descent datum, 𝓜_d|U_d°=L_d°, and at a geometric point D=Σn_x x its stalk is ⊗_x F_x^{⊗n_x}: one-dimensional when the inertia character at every point of R∩supp D is trivial, zero otherwise. Notation: U=X−R with j:U→X; X_d=Sym^dX with the finite quotient map q_d:X^d→X_d; U_d°⊂X_d is the open of multiplicity-free divisors supported in U and (U^d)°=q_d⁻¹(U_d°) the ordered distinct points of U; ω_d:X_d^√R→X_d is the coarse map (GC.1/root-symmetric-coarse), an isomorphism over Sym^dU, so U_d° is open in X_d^√R.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

Constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaves on schemes of finite type over k and k̄, with finite pushforward and proper base change, are the scheme theory requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (upstream EtaleCohomologyFoundations).
proofSteps: q_d is finite and S_d-invariant, and F^{⊠d} is S_d-equivariant by permuting factors; take the image of the averaging idempotent in the abelian category of constructible Q̄ℓ-sheaves on X_d (GC.3/averaging-exactness).

Stalks: proper base change for the finite q_d identifies (q_{d*}F^{⊠d})_D with the sum over the reduced ordered preimages of D (étale cohomology ignores the nilpotent structure of the finite fibre); S_d permutes them transitively with stabilizer ∏_x S_{n_x}, and a permutation acts trivially on a tensor power of a line, so the invariants are ⊗_xF_x^{⊗n_x}.
F_x for x∈R is the inertia invariants of L_x̄, which is the whole line or zero (IG.1/decomposition-inertia; GC.3/root-curve-character-dictionary).
Over U_d° the map q_d is the S_d-torsor and F=L, so 𝓜_d|U_d° is the descent L_d°.

For the subsheaf assertion, use local finite quadratic root charts f:Y→X: the pullback of L is lisse on the regular chart Y, and F=j_*L is the μ₂-invariant summand of f_*L_Y. On products of these charts, the same finite-pushforward and commuting-projector description applies to F^{⊠d}. Restriction of a lisse sheaf on a normal chart to the dense distinct-point open is injective; finite pushforward and invariant summands preserve this injection. Hence F^{⊠d} and then 𝓜_d inject into the direct images of their distinct-point restrictions. Maps f^{⊠d}, followed by q_* and the invariant projector, give functoriality and its identity/composition laws.
acceptance: 𝓜_0=Q̄ℓ on X_0=Spec k and 𝓜_1=j_*L.
If χ is unramified at every x∈R, F is the lisse extension of L to X and 𝓜_d is Deligne's lisse symmetric-power system on X_d.
X=P¹, R={0,∞}, χ the quadratic Kummer character: the stalks of 𝓜_2 at 2·0, at 0+∞ and at 0+y with y∈U vanish, and the stalk at y+y′ with y,y′∈U is a line.

nodes.title: Cohomology of a geometrically nontrivial twisted curve sheaf
nodes.statement: If L is geometrically nontrivial, that is, χ is nontrivial on π1(U⊗k̄), then H⁰(X⊗k̄,j_*L)=0 and H²(X⊗k̄,j_*L)=0, so H*(X⊗k̄,j_*L) is concentrated in degree one, Frobenius-equivariantly. By GC.3/rational-coarse-comparison for d=1 the same holds for H*(X_1^√R⊗k̄,L).
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.
proofSteps: H⁰(X_k̄,j_*L)=H⁰(U_k̄,L) is the invariants of π1(U_k̄) on a line on which it acts by the nontrivial character χ, hence zero (IG.0/etale-fundamental-group).

Poincaré duality for j_* coefficients on the smooth projective curve X_k̄ (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2/curve-poincare-duality-with-j-star-statement) pairs H²(X_k̄,j_*L) perfectly with H⁰(X_k̄,j_*L^∨(1)); L^∨ has the geometrically nontrivial character χ⁻¹, so this group vanishes.

The scheme cohomological-dimension bound gives H^i(X_k̄,j_*L)=0 for i>2, and negative degrees vanish for an ordinary sheaf (SF.2, integrating EtaleCohomologyFoundations §F.3 and §F.4.5). The cited duality statement is used over a finite coefficient field E/Qℓ and extended flatly to Q̄ℓ; no integral or torsion duality is used.
Apply GC.3/rational-coarse-comparison for d=1 to transfer the concentration statement to the root curve.
acceptance: The constant sheaf is excluded: on P¹ it has H⁰ and H² nonzero.
A geometrically trivial χ with χ(Frob)=ζ₃ is excluded: H⁰(X_k̄,L) is a line.
X=P¹, R={0,∞}, χ quadratic Kummer: H¹ vanishes too, so all cohomology is zero and ∧^dH¹=0 for d≥1.

nodes.title: Comparison with the symmetric pushforward description
nodes.statement: The local system 𝕃_d of GC.3/monodromy-symmetric-local-system is canonically isomorphic, compatibly with Frobenius, to the S_d-invariant part (p_{d,!}L^{⊠d})^{S_d} of the proper pushforward along the ordered map p_d:(X_1^√R)^d→X_d^√R (GC.1/ordered-divisors), which is the parent definition GC.3/symmetric-local-system; in particular the latter is concentrated in degree zero and is a rank-one local system.
hypotheses: For GC layers: k is finite of characteristic p≠2; X/k is smooth, projective and geometrically connected; R⊂X is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty; ρ=deg R, and g is the curve genus. Coefficients are Q̄ℓ with ℓ≠p; geometric Frobenius is used.

p_d is proper and quasi-finite but not representable at collisions of branch points: on stabilizers it is multiplication μ₂^m→μ₂ (GC.1/ordered-proper; EGC3-2). Proper base change for such morphisms of tame Deligne–Mumford stacks with Q̄ℓ coefficients is gap GC3-STACK-PUSHFORWARD.
proofSteps: p_d^*𝕃_d and L^{⊠d} are rank-one local systems on the connected normal stack (X_1^√R)^d that agree on the dense open (U^d)°, S_d-equivariantly, so they are isomorphic (IG.5/finite-cover-image-lemmas); adjunction gives an S_d-invariant map 𝕃_d→p_{d*}L^{⊠d}=p_{d,!}L^{⊠d}.

At D=Σn_xx, proper base change and nilpotent invariance (GC3-STACK-PUSHFORWARD) reduce the geometric fibre to a finite groupoid. Each orbit of orderings has relative stabilizer ∏_{x∈R∩supp D}ker(μ₂^{n_x}→μ₂); the residual-gerbe maps are the products [pt/μ₂]^{n_x}→[pt/μ₂]. The unreduced fibre is not asserted to equal these gerbes (RS.1/closed-fibre; EGC3-5). The tensor character is trivial on this finite kernel, so higher cohomology vanishes; S_d acts transitively on the orderings, with unsigned tensor permutation acting trivially on their lines. Thus the invariant stalk is one line in degree zero.

The adjunction unit on this invariant stalk identifies the source line with the same kernel-invariant line, hence is nonzero and is an isomorphism. The higher target stalks vanish, so the map is an isomorphism of complexes, compatibly with Frobenius.
acceptance: d=1: p_1 is the identity and both sides are L.
Over U_d° both sides are L_d°, by Galois descent along the S_d-torsor.
At 2x with x∈R the fibre is [pt/μ₂]²→[pt/μ₂] by multiplication; a representable-finite pushforward theorem does not apply there.
